title: Simple Machines and Power
seo_title: Grade 5 Science: Simple Machines and Power Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Machines transfer force and energy: simple machines (lever, wedge, inclined plane, wheel and axle, pulley, screw), compound machines, natural machines such as the musculoskeletal system, and power as the rate of energy transfer. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Science 5, Physics)
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 science worksheets (BC): levers, pulleys, gears, inclined planes, wedges and screws, mechanical advantage, work and power. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Simple machines change the size or direction of a force.
key_sub: Less force over a longer distance.
body_html:
How to think about it

The six simple machines are the lever, wedge, inclined plane, wheel and axle, pulley and screw. They make work easier by changing the size or direction of a force: a ramp lets you use less force over a longer distance.

Compound machines, like a bicycle, combine simple machines. Your arm is a natural lever. Power is how fast energy is transferred: a more powerful motor does the same work in less time.

Example

Which simple machine is a ramp?

A sloping surface

Answer: an inclined plane

Example

A single fixed pulley on a flagpole: what does it change?

You pull down, the flag goes up.

Answer: the direction of the force

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a machine reduces the work done (it reduces the force).
  • Mixing up a wedge and an inclined plane.
  • Thinking power and force are the same.

faq.q: Why is a door handle far from the hinges?
faq.a: A longer lever arm needs less force to turn the door.
The rate of transferring energy, measured in watts.

items.q: What is the effort in a pulley system?
items.e: Effort is the force that makes the machine work.

items.q: Two gears are meshed. The first turns clockwise. Which way does the second turn?
items.e: Meshed gears turn in opposite directions.

items.q: What is a mechanism?
c: a set of moving parts that work together to do a job
items.e: Gears, pulleys and levers can make mechanisms.

items.q: What is a load in a machine?
c: the object being moved or lifted
items.e: The effort moves the load.

items.q: Which everyday object is a lever?
items.e: A seesaw turns on a pivot.

items.q: 3 gears are meshed in a row: A → B → C. Gear A turns counterclockwise. Which way does gear C turn?
items.e: Each meshed gear turns the opposite way to the one before it. With 3 gears, gear C turns counterclockwise.

items.q: A clock has many gears. Why?
c: so the hands turn at different speeds
items.e: Gears of different sizes turn at different speeds.

items.q: Which machine changes a small turning force at the handle into a big force at the axle?
c: a wheel and axle, like a doorknob
items.e: The big wheel makes turning easier.

items.q: What kind of mechanism is used in a well bucket on a rope?
items.e: Levers, pulleys and gears are simple machines.

items.q: Which machine uses gears?
items.e: Turning the handle turns gears that spin the beaters.

items.q: Why do conveyor belts in a factory use pulleys?
c: the belt runs over pulleys that keep it moving
items.e: Belts and pulleys move objects.

items.q: In a pulley system, why does the effort get smaller with more ropes?
c: The load is shared between the ropes.
items.e: But you pull more rope.

items.q: Which design makes the effort smaller in a pulley system?
c: tying the rope to the load only
using more pulleys and more rope sections to hold the load
items.e: More supporting ropes share the load.

items.q: What is a mechanism?
c: a device that makes a force have a bigger effect or changes its direction
items.e: Levers, pulleys and gears.

items.q: Which design would make a model crane lift a heavier load?
c: add a second pulley to share the load
make the arm out of paper
items.e: More pulleys reduce the force needed.

items.q: What kind of mechanism is used in a bottle opener?
items.e: Levers, pulleys and gears are simple machines.

items.q: 5 gears are meshed in a row: A → B → C → D → E. Gear A turns counterclockwise. Which way does gear E turn?
items.e: Each meshed gear turns the opposite way to the one before it. With 5 gears, gear E turns counterclockwise.

items.q: What happens when two gears touch and one turns?
c: The other turns the opposite way.
The other turns the same way.
items.e: Teeth push each other.

items.q: Which simple machine is a wheel with a rope that can be fixed or movable?
items.e: Pulleys can be fixed or movable.

items.q: Why does a big gear driven by a small gear turn more slowly?
c: Gears always turn at the same speed.
It has more teeth, so the small gear must turn more times for one big turn.
items.e: Count the teeth.

items.q: A small gear with 20 teeth drives a big gear with 60 teeth. How many times does the small gear turn while the big gear turns 4 times?
items.e: 60 ÷ 20 = 3 small turns for each big turn.

items.q: Which simple machine is made of a rope over a grooved wheel?
items.e: That is the definition of a pulley.

items.q: A 16-tooth gear drives a 48-tooth gear. The big gear turns 3 times. How many times does the small gear turn?
items.e: Each turn of the big gear moves 48 teeth, which is 3 turns of the small gear. 3 × 3 = 9.

items.q: A 30-tooth gear drives a 90-tooth gear. The big gear turns 5 times. How many times does the small gear turn?
items.e: Each turn of the big gear moves 90 teeth, which is 3 turns of the small gear. 5 × 3 = 15.

items.q: A small gear with 15 teeth drives a big gear with 60 teeth. How many times does the small gear turn while the big gear turns 1 time?
items.e: 60 ÷ 15 = 4 small turns for each big turn.

items.q: Gear A (15 teeth) turns clockwise and drives gear B (45 teeth). Which way does gear B turn?
items.e: Two gears that touch turn in opposite directions.

items.q: A 30-tooth gear drives a 60-tooth gear. The small gear turns 6 times. How many times does the big gear turn?
items.e: The big gear has 2 times as many teeth, so it turns 2 times more slowly. 6 ÷ 2 = 3.

items.q: On a bike, what links the pedal gear to the back-wheel gear?
items.e: Gears linked by a chain turn the same way.

items.q: Why does a sailboat use pulleys on its ropes?
c: so sailors can pull the sails with less force
items.e: Pulley blocks make the work easier.

items.q: A 15-tooth gear drives a 45-tooth gear. The big gear turns 1 time. How many times does the small gear turn?
items.e: Each turn of the big gear moves 45 teeth, which is 3 turns of the small gear. 1 × 3 = 3.

items.q: 3 gears are meshed in a row: A → B → C. Gear A turns clockwise. Which way does gear C turn?
items.e: Each meshed gear turns the opposite way to the one before it. With 3 gears, gear C turns clockwise.

items.q: A 16-tooth gear drives a 64-tooth gear. The big gear turns 1 time. How many times does the small gear turn?
items.e: Each turn of the big gear moves 64 teeth, which is 4 turns of the small gear. 1 × 4 = 4.

items.q: 4 gears are meshed in a row: A → B → C → D. Gear A turns counterclockwise. Which way does gear D turn?
items.e: Each meshed gear turns the opposite way to the one before it. With 4 gears, gear D turns clockwise.

items.q: A 8-tooth gear drives a 24-tooth gear. The big gear turns 1 time. How many times does the small gear turn?
items.e: Each turn of the big gear moves 24 teeth, which is 3 turns of the small gear. 1 × 3 = 3.

items.q: A 24-tooth gear drives a 72-tooth gear. The small gear turns 9 times. How many times does the big gear turn?
items.e: The big gear has 3 times as many teeth, so it turns 3 times more slowly. 9 ÷ 3 = 3.

items.q: A small gear with 12 teeth drives a big gear with 24 teeth. The small gear turns 6 times. How many times does the big gear turn?
A small gear with 20 teeth drives a big gear with 60 teeth. The small gear turns 3 times. How many times does the big gear turn?
A small gear with 10 teeth drives a big gear with 40 teeth. How many times does the small gear turn while the big gear turns 2 times?
items.e: 40 ÷ 10 = 4 small turns for each big turn.

items.q: A 8-tooth gear drives a 32-tooth gear. The small gear turns 12 times. How many times does the big gear turn?
items.e: The big gear has 4 times as many teeth, so it turns 4 times more slowly. 12 ÷ 4 = 3.

items.q: A 8-tooth gear drives a 24-tooth gear. The small gear turns 3 times. How many times does the big gear turn?
items.e: The big gear has 3 times as many teeth, so it turns 3 times more slowly. 3 ÷ 3 = 1.

items.q: What kind of mechanism is used in a mechanical clock?
items.e: Levers, pulleys and gears are simple machines.

items.q: What does a single fixed pulley do?
c: It changes the direction of the force.
items.e: You pull down to lift up.

items.q: A small gear with 10 teeth drives a big gear with 30 teeth. How do they compare?
c: The big gear turns backward and faster.
The big gear turns more slowly.
Both turn at the same speed.
items.e: The small gear turns 3 times for each turn of the big gear.

items.q: What happens to the speed of a load lifted with many pulleys?
c: It rises more slowly because you pull more rope.
items.e: Force is reduced, distance is increased.

items.q: What is friction's effect in a machine?
c: It slows moving parts and wastes some energy as heat.
items.e: Oil reduces friction.

items.q: A 12-tooth gear drives a 36-tooth gear. The small gear turns 3 times. How many times does the big gear turn?
items.e: The big gear has 3 times as many teeth, so it turns 3 times more slowly. 3 ÷ 3 = 1.

items.q: A 10-tooth gear drives a 30-tooth gear. The small gear turns 3 times. How many times does the big gear turn?
items.e: The big gear has 3 times as many teeth, so it turns 3 times more slowly. 3 ÷ 3 = 1.

items.q: What is a gear?
items.e: Gear teeth fit together.

items.q: 2 gears are meshed in a row: A → B. Gear A turns counterclockwise. Which way does gear B turn?
items.e: Each meshed gear turns the opposite way to the one before it. With 2 gears, gear B turns clockwise.

items.q: Why do car engines use belts and pulleys?
c: to turn other parts, like the fan, with the engine's motion
items.e: Belts carry motion between pulleys.

items.q: Which mechanism changes turning motion into up-and-down motion in a toy?
items.e: Cams are used in moving toys.

items.q: Which is an example of a pulley in daily life?
c: window blinds pulled up with a cord
items.e: The cord runs over small pulleys.

items.q: What kind of mechanism is used in a flagpole rope?
items.e: Levers, pulleys and gears are simple machines.

items.q: Why do people oil the gears of a bike?
c: to reduce friction so they turn easily
items.e: Less friction, less wear.

items.q: Three gears are in a row: A → B → C. A turns clockwise. Which way does C turn?
items.e: Each meshed gear reverses direction: A clockwise, B counterclockwise, C clockwise.

items.q: Why do some gear systems use a very big gear driven by a tiny gear?
c: to make the big gear spin faster
to make the big gear turn with more force
items.e: A slow big gear turns with more force.

items.q: What kind of mechanism is used in a bicycle chain and sprockets?
items.e: Levers, pulleys and gears are simple machines.

items.q: 4 gears are meshed in a row: A → B → C → D. Gear A turns clockwise. Which way does gear D turn?
items.e: Each meshed gear turns the opposite way to the one before it. With 4 gears, gear D turns counterclockwise.

items.q: 5 gears are meshed in a row: A → B → C → D → E. Gear A turns clockwise. Which way does gear E turn?
items.e: Each meshed gear turns the opposite way to the one before it. With 5 gears, gear E turns clockwise.

items.q: Gear A has 12 teeth and gear B has 36 teeth. Gear B turns once. How many times does gear A turn?
A ball dropped with 60 J of potential energy bounces back up with 30 J. Where did the rest of the energy go?
c: It was converted to thermal and sound energy.
It became new mass in the ball.
It was stored in the ground forever as potential energy.
items.e: Energy is not destroyed: 30 J is converted to thermal and sound energy.

items.q: A light bulb receives 80 J of electrical energy and gives out 10 J of light energy. How much energy is converted to thermal energy?
items.e: Total energy out = total energy in: 80 − 10 = 70 J.

items.q: A furnace system has a thermostat. What does the thermostat do?
c: It senses the temperature and switches the furnace on or off.
items.e: It controls the system with feedback.

items.q: Why can no machine be 100% efficient?
c: Some energy is always lost, mostly as heat from friction.
items.e: Lubrication reduces friction.

items.q: Why do ramps make it easier to move a wheelchair up a step?
c: A longer slope means less force is needed (but over a longer distance).
items.e: Inclined planes trade distance for force.

items.q: What is the output of a system?
items.e: Forward motion is the output of a bike.

items.q: What is efficiency?
c: the percentage of input energy that becomes useful output
items.e: No machine is 100% efficient.

items.q: A ball has 200 J of gravitational potential energy at the top of a fall. Ignoring air resistance, how much kinetic energy does it have just before it hits the ground?
items.e: Energy is conserved: all the potential energy becomes kinetic energy.

items.q: What is a system?
c: a group of parts that work together to do a job
items.e: A bicycle is a mechanical system.

items.q: Noah pushes a box with a force of 25 N for 1.5 m. How much work is done?
items.e: work done = force × distance = 25 × 1.5 = 37.5 J.

items.q: Ava does 40 J of work moving a load with a force of 40 N. How far does the load move?
items.e: distance = work ÷ force = 40 ÷ 40.

items.q: A student pushes a box with a force of 80 N for 3 m. How much work is done?
items.e: Work = force × distance = 80 N × 3 m = 240 J.

items.q: A ball has 100 J of gravitational potential energy at the top of a fall. Ignoring air resistance, how much kinetic energy does it have just before it hits the ground?
items.e: Energy is conserved: all the potential energy becomes kinetic energy.

items.q: Benjamin pushes a cart with a force of 10 N for 1.5 m. How much work is done?
items.e: work done = force × distance = 10 × 1.5 = 15 J.

items.q: Priya lifts a crate with a force of 100 N for 0.5 m. How much work is done?
items.e: work done = force × distance = 100 × 0.5 = 50 J.

items.q: A student pushes a box with a force of 20 N for 5 m. How much work is done?
items.e: Work = force × distance = 20 N × 5 m = 100 J.

items.q: Which simple machine is a wedge?
items.e: A wedge splits things apart.

items.q: Nathan pushes a cart with a force of 50 N for 1.5 m. How much work is done?
items.e: work done = force × distance = 50 × 1.5 = 75 J.

items.q: A student pushes a box with a force of 60 N for 10 m. How much work is done?
items.e: Work = force × distance = 60 N × 10 m = 600 J.

items.q: A student pushes a box with a force of 50 N for 10 m. How much work is done?
items.e: Work = force × distance = 50 N × 10 m = 500 J.

items.q: A lever lifts a load of 200 N with an effort of 25 N. What is its mechanical advantage?
items.e: Mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort = 200 ÷ 25 = 8.

items.q: A machine uses 500 J of energy (work in) and does 450 J of useful work (work out). What is its efficiency?
items.e: Efficiency = work out ÷ work in × 100% = 450 ÷ 500 × 100% = 90%.

items.q: Which is an environmental cost of a transportation system?
c: air pollution and greenhouse gases from vehicles
items.e: Public transit can reduce the cost.

items.q: A force of 50 N is applied to a crowbar 1.5 m from the pivot. What is the moment?
items.e: moment = force × distance from pivot = 50 × 1.5.

items.q: A force of 40 N is applied to a lever 1.5 m from the pivot. What is the moment?
items.e: moment = force × distance from pivot = 40 × 1.5.

items.q: A machine uses 400 J of energy (work in) and does 300 J of useful work (work out). What is its efficiency?
items.e: Efficiency = work out ÷ work in × 100% = 300 ÷ 400 × 100% = 75%.

items.q: Mei (weight 500 N) sits 1 m from the pivot of a see-saw. Priya weighs 200 N. How far from the pivot on the other side must Priya sit to balance it?
items.e: Balanced: 500 × 1 = 200 × d, so d = 2.5 m. The lighter person sits further away.

items.q: Mateo (weight 450 N) sits 1 m from the pivot of a see-saw. Zoe weighs 300 N. How far from the pivot on the other side must Zoe sit to balance it?
items.e: Balanced: 450 × 1 = 300 × d, so d = 1.5 m. The lighter person sits further away.

items.q: A force of 60 N is applied to a crowbar 0.2 m from the pivot. What is the moment?
items.e: moment = force × distance from pivot = 60 × 0.2.

items.q: Ava (weight 300 N) sits 1 m from the pivot of a see-saw. Aiden weighs 250 N. How far from the pivot on the other side must Aiden sit to balance it?
items.e: Balanced: 300 × 1 = 250 × d, so d = 1.2 m. The lighter person sits further away.

items.q: A force of 50 N is applied to a crowbar 0.2 m from the pivot. What is the moment?
items.e: moment = force × distance from pivot = 50 × 0.2.

items.q: A lever lifts a load of 100 N with an effort of 25 N. What is its mechanical advantage?
items.e: Mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort = 100 ÷ 25 = 4.

items.q: A lever lifts a load of 150 N with an effort of 50 N. What is its mechanical advantage?
items.e: Mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort = 150 ÷ 50 = 3.

items.q: A lever lifts a load of 200 N with an effort of 50 N. What is its mechanical advantage?
items.e: Mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort = 200 ÷ 50 = 4.

items.q: Benjamin (weight 400 N) sits 2 m from the pivot of a see-saw. Liam weighs 250 N. How far from the pivot on the other side must Liam sit to balance it?
items.e: Balanced: 400 × 2 = 250 × d, so d = 3.2 m. The lighter person sits further away.

items.q: A lever lifts a load of 40 N with an effort of 10 N. What is its mechanical advantage?
items.e: Mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort = 40 ÷ 10 = 4.

items.q: A student pushes a box with a force of 40 N for 2 m. How much work is done?
items.e: Work = force × distance = 40 N × 2 m = 80 J.

items.q: A lever lifts a load of 80 N with an effort of 40 N. What is its mechanical advantage?
items.e: Mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort = 80 ÷ 40 = 2.

items.q: A lever lifts a load of 320 N with an effort of 40 N. What is its mechanical advantage?
items.e: Mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort = 320 ÷ 40 = 8.

items.q: A student pushes a box with a force of 40 N for 3 m. How much work is done?
items.e: Work = force × distance = 40 N × 3 m = 120 J.
